newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Villagers in Bangladesh attack African students.
newsitem.headline: Villagers in Bangladesh attack African students.

text.p: African students at a technical institute near Dhaka began boycotting classes on Wednesday after two of their colleagues were injured in an assault they alleged was racially motivated.

Ibrahim Bande, chairman of the African Students Union at the Islamic Institute of Technology at Tongi, 25 km (15 miles) from the Bangladesh capital, said the Africans felt insecure following the attack by villagers on two Senegalese students on Tuesday night.
Abdoulie Gieng and Usman (one name) suffered severe head injuries, Bande said. Both were admitted to hospital.
"They faced a racial attack by local people as they ventured to a market outside the campus," he told Reuters by telephone.
Professor Abdul Matin Patwari, director general of the institute, confirmed "minor clashes" between students and outsiders but dismissed allegations they were racially motivated.
"The information I got was that the clashes occurred over price bargaining during shopping. Not that people attacked only because they are black," he told Reuters.
"They are from totally different cultures. So there might be some misunderstanding and suspicion," he added.
Patwari said he had spoken to local community leaders in an attempt to prevent further incidents.
Patwari said he had called in police to guard the campus.
The 70 African students at the institute camped out at the gates throughout the night to protest against the attack, and on Wednesday announced an indefinite boycott of classes.
"This is not the first time we were attacked. We won't attend classes until the authorities can ensure our security," said Bande, a Gambian.
"We are facing racial discrimination both within and outside (the campus). We need to go out for shopping but the local people often tease us...," he said.
He added that the Africans were subject to racist slurs and harassment, "...and the authorities say they can't do anything."
He said students from Somalia and Gabon had previously been harassed.
Bande said the students would march to the office of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to lodge complaints.
"We will seek protection from harassment and insecurity. If we can't get it, we will rather ask for tickets to our homes ... the situation is absolutely unacceptable," he said.
